description_md: One row per physical sampling event at its native grain (site, tow, net, cast, bottle, underway, transect, region pool). An adjacency list: `parent_sample_key` points at the containing event and `root_sample_key` at the top of the chain, so counting distinct events at any level is a single `GROUP BY`.
Globally unique event key, namespaced `dataset_key:sample_type:id` so the same integer id in two datasets — or at two event levels in one dataset — never collides.
Event grain: `site`, `tow`, `net`, `cast`, `bottle`, `underway`, `transect` or `region_pool`.
The containing event (net → tow → site; bottle → cast). NULL at the top of the chain. Flat adjacency list: attributes are not inherited.
Top of this event's containment chain; equals `sample_key` for single-level datasets. Use `count(DISTINCT root_sample_key)` to count stations/casts irrespective of grain.
Provenance stamp: `provider_dataset`.
CalCOFI station grid cell. NULL where the dataset has no station assignment (region-pooled phytoplankton).

CalCOFI station natural key as the source records it (line/station, e.g. `090.0 060.0`). Present on 13 of the 18 source event tables, so it is carried on the event dimension rather than lost to consolidation; `grid_key` is the derived grid cell, this is the source's own station id.
CalCOFI cruise natural key `YYYY-MM-NODC`.
Order in which the station was occupied on the cruise. Source spelling varies (`order_occ`, `ord_occ`) and CTD stores it as text; normalised to an integer here.
Event latitude (WGS84).
Event longitude (WGS84).
Event start time (UTC).
Shallowest depth sampled by this event.
Deepest depth sampled by this event.
Net gear code where the dataset records one (C1/CB/CV/PV oblique or vertical, MT manta); NULL for gears and datasets without one. Needed to compute gear-appropriate CPUE.
Point geometry minted from `longitude`/`latitude` (OGC:CRS84).

The occurrence-headline long table: one scalar measurement per row, environmental (`realm = 'env'`) and biological (`realm = 'bio'`) together. Biological taxon is the global `taxon_key`; sub-occurrence detail (length/stage bins, behavior) lives in `obs_attribute`, and event-level effort in `sample_measurement`.
Surrogate key, renumbered globally when the release concatenates the per-dataset shards.
`env` for physical/chemical measurements, `bio` for organism observations.
Provenance stamp: `provider_dataset`.
The sampling event this observation came from; joins `sample`.
CalCOFI station grid cell, denormalized from `sample` so rollups need no join. NULL for region-pooled data.
Cruise, denormalized from `sample` so rollups need no join.
Observation latitude (WGS84).
Observation longitude (WGS84).
Observation time (UTC). NULL for region-pooled data with no event time.
Shallowest depth this observation represents.
Deepest depth this observation represents; equal to `depth_min_m` for point measurements (bottle, CTD scan).
Global taxon key, `worms:<AphiaID>` or `itis:<TSN>` for birds. NULL for `env` rows. Joins `taxon`.
Life stage where the source resolves one (larva, adult, juvenile, egg, phyllosoma).
Measured quantity; joins the `measurement_type` vocabulary.
The measured value, in the units `measurement_type` declares.
Source quality flag, verbatim.
Source-reported precision where available.
H3 cell at resolution 10, stored as UBIGINT. Aggregate coarser at query time with `h3_cell_to_parent(hex_id, res)` — there is no per-resolution column ladder.

Sub-occurrence attribution: the breakdown *within* an `obs` headline row. Covers numeric frequency distributions (length bins, stage numbers) and categorical breakdowns (seabird behavior). Counts here sum to the headline where the source is internally consistent.
Surrogate key.
Provenance stamp: `provider_dataset`.
The sampling event; joins `sample`.
Global taxon key; joins `taxon`.
Life stage the attribution applies to.
The attribute being broken down: `body_length`, `stage` or `behavior`.
Numeric bin — length in mm, stage number. NULL for categorical attributes.
Category label — stage description, behavior name. NULL for purely numeric bins.
Number of individuals in this bin.
Source quality flag, verbatim.

Event-level (effort) measurements: quantities that describe the sampling event itself rather than anything observed in it — net volume filtered, standard haul factor, proportion sorted, bottle cast conditions. Kept apart from `obs` so effort is never mistaken for an observation.
Surrogate key.
The sampling event this effort measurement describes; joins `sample`.
Provenance stamp: `provider_dataset`.
Measured quantity; joins the `measurement_type` vocabulary.
The measured value, in the units `measurement_type` declares.
Source quality flag, verbatim.

Supplemental full-resolution CTD scans, identical in shape to `obs`. Excluded from the default table list and the ERD because of its size; opt in with `cc_get_db(supplemental = TRUE)`. The default `obs` carries CTD via the adaptively thinned `ctd_thin`.

One authoritative row per taxon, keyed by `taxon_key` = `worms:<AphiaID>` (or `itis:<TSN>` for birds). Replaces the per-dataset taxon tables; duplicates across datasets collapse to one row, with names and lineage coalesced by source priority.
Global taxon key: lowercase authority prefix plus id, `worms:127023` or `itis:176754`.
WoRMS AphiaID.
ITIS Taxonomic Serial Number.
GBIF backbone taxon key.
NCBI Taxonomy id.
iNaturalist taxon id.
Accepted scientific name.
Common name where one is recorded.
Taxonomic rank.
Ordinal for sorting ranks from kingdom down.
WoRMS status (accepted, unaccepted, ...).
Lineage parent; walk this to expand a taxon to its descendants.
Kingdom.
Phylum.
Class.
Order (named `order_taxon` because `order` is a SQL keyword).
Family.

Crosswalk from each dataset's own taxon vocabulary to the global `taxon_key`. `obs` resolves its taxon by joining this on (`dataset_key`, `ds_taxa_code`), so a dataset can keep its local codes without leaking them into the shared model.
Key of this crosswalk row, `<dataset-or-known-list>:<local code>`.
The dataset whose vocabulary this row belongs to.
The global taxon it resolves to; joins `taxon`.
Scientific name as the source dataset spells it.
Common name as the source dataset spells it.
The dataset's own code, as stored on its measurement rows.
Portable groupings of taxa (phytoplankton functional groups, seabirds, marine mammals). Many taxa per group; a taxon may belong to several.
Group key, `<dataset-or-known-list>:<group>`.
Human-readable description of the group.
A member taxon; joins `taxon`.
